chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 518: Li Huowang Stalks the Empress - The Bodhisattva's Gaze
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang stalks the Empress Dowager and Eldest Princess to a mountain temple. Invisible and ready to strike, he witnesses a shocking act of filial piety that changes everything.
og_title: The Assassin Waits: Li Huowang Faces the Temple Trap
og_description: Silence. Suspense. A young monk carried to a queen’s bed. Li Huowang's assassination plan takes a dangerous detour in this tense chapter.
twitter_title: Stalking a Queen in the Shadows of a Giant God
twitter_description: Invisible and waiting, Li Huowang watches a family’s dark secret unfold, just as he prepares for the kill.

lore_anchors.definition: In Buddhism, a being who delays their own enlightenment to help all sentient beings. In the Dao-Twisted World, even this compassionate figure is depicted with a male form, a subtle but powerful twist on tradition.
The title of the mother of the reigning emperor. In Chinese imperial politics, she often holds immense, if unofficial, power, frequently acting as a regent behind the throne.
The title for the emperor's elder sister or aunt. A high-ranking member of the imperial court with significant political influence.
The young emperor of Great Liang. He has allied himself with Li Huowang to purge his family of corrupting influences.
Palace maids, often low-born women selected for service in the imperial harem and court; their loyalty is a fluid commodity in a world of power struggles.
A castrated male servant of the imperial court. Historically, eunuchs could rise to immense power, serving as the emperor’s most trusted (and often most corrupt) confidantes.

The core Confucian virtue demanding absolute respect, obedience, and care for one’s parents and elders. In the Dao-Twisted World, this sacred duty is often twisted into a justification for the most monstrous acts.
